sentiment.rationale: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.30-$6.40 from $6.00-$6.20, and cash flow from operations guidance was raised to at least $7.5B from approximately $7.0B. The Health Care Benefits segment showed strong improvement (adjusted operating income +39.4% y/y), and the Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segment delivered another strong quarter. However, the Health Services segment guidance was reduced by ~$200M due to Oak Street pressure, and management maintained a cautious outlook on medical cost trends and the consumer environment, preventing a higher score.

summary.revenue: Second quarter total revenues of $98.9B, up 8.4% compared to prior year.
summary.eps: Second quarter GAAP diluted EPS of $0.80, down from $1.41; Adjusted EPS of $1.81, relatively consistent with prior year.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $6.30-$6.40 from $6.00-$6.20. Full-year total revenues expected to be at least $391.5B. Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income expected to be approximately $2.42B. Health Services adjusted operating income expected to be at least $7.34B. Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness adjusted operating income expected to be at least $5.68B. Cash flow from operations expected to be at least $7.5B.
summary.margin: Health Care Benefits segment MBR of 89.9% for Q2 2025, up 30 bps from prior year. Full-year 2025 MBR expected to be approximately 91% at the low end of guidance.
key_risks: Elevated medical cost trends across all lines of business, particularly in Group Medicare Advantage (triggered a $470M premium deficiency reserve).
Pressure in Health Care Delivery business driven by higher medical benefit ratio at Oak Street Health.
Continued pharmacy reimbursement pressure in the Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segment.
Cautious outlook on Part D due to substantial changes in plan liability from the Inflation Reduction Act.
Potential changes in vaccine market demand and consumer environment in the back half of the year.
key_opportunities: Strong start to the 2026 PBM selling season with retention expected in the high-90s.
Meaningful progress in Aetna margin recovery, with adjusted operating income up 39.4% y/y in Q2.
CVS CostVantage model transitioning commercial scripts in line with expectations, with government transition planned for 2026.
Growth in Oak Street at-risk membership (up 31% y/y) and strong volumes at Signify Health.
Market disruption from other pharmacy closures driving script share gains (retail pharmacy script share up 60 bps to 27.8%).

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management uses language like 'we are pleased to report another consecutive quarter of solid results,' 'we are encouraged by our enterprise performance and revised outlook,' and 'we are building momentum,' while also maintaining a 'prudent and respectful outlook for the remainder of the year.'
